nodes.Name: fixLongPath
nodes.DocComment: fixLongPath is a noop on non-Windows platforms.

nodes.Name: file
nodes.DocComment:
file is the real representation of *File.
The extra level of indirection ensures that no clients of os
can overwrite this data, which could cause the finalizer
to close the wrong file descriptor.

Fields.Name: appendMode
Fields.DocComment: whether file is opened for appending

nodes.Name: fd
nodes.DocComment: fd is the Plan 9 implementation of Fd.

nodes.Name: newFileFromNewFile
nodes.DocComment: newFileFromNewFile is called by [NewFile].

nodes.Name: dirInfo
nodes.DocComment: Auxiliary information if the File describes a directory

Fields.Name: nbuf
Fields.DocComment: length of buf; return value from Read

Fields.Name: bufp
Fields.DocComment: location of next record in buf.

nodes.Name: DevNull
nodes.DocComment:
DevNull is the name of the operating system's “null device.”
On Unix-like systems, it is "/dev/null"; on Windows, "NUL".

nodes.Name: syscallMode
nodes.DocComment: syscallMode returns the syscall-specific mode bits from Go's portable mode bits.

nodes.Name: openFileNolog
nodes.DocComment: openFileNolog is the Plan 9 implementation of OpenFile.

nodes.Name: Close
nodes.DocComment:
Close closes the File, rendering it unusable for I/O.
On files that support SetDeadline, any pending I/O operations will
be canceled and return immediately with an ErrClosed error.
Close will return an error if it has already been called.

nodes.Name: destroy
nodes.DocComment:
destroy actually closes the descriptor. This is called when
there are no remaining references, by the decref, readUnlock,
and writeUnlock methods.

nodes.Name: Stat
nodes.DocComment:
Stat returns the FileInfo structure describing file.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

nodes.Name: Truncate
nodes.DocComment:
Truncate changes the size of the file.
It does not change the I/O offset.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

nodes.Name: Sync
nodes.DocComment:
Sync commits the current contents of the file to stable storage.
Typically, this means flushing the file system's in-memory copy
of recently written data to disk.

nodes.Name: read
nodes.DocComment:
read reads up to len(b) bytes from the File.
It returns the number of bytes read and an error, if any.

nodes.Name: pread
nodes.DocComment:
pread reads len(b) bytes from the File starting at byte offset off.
It returns the number of bytes read and the error, if any.
EOF is signaled by a zero count with err set to nil.

nodes.Name: write
nodes.DocComment:
write writes len(b) bytes to the File.
It returns the number of bytes written and an error, if any.
Since Plan 9 preserves message boundaries, never allow
a zero-byte write.

nodes.Name: pwrite
nodes.DocComment:
pwrite writes len(b) bytes to the File starting at byte offset off.
It returns the number of bytes written and an error, if any.
Since Plan 9 preserves message boundaries, never allow
a zero-byte write.

nodes.Name: seek
nodes.DocComment:
seek sets the offset for the next Read or Write on file to offset, interpreted
according to whence: 0 means relative to the origin of the file, 1 means
relative to the current offset, and 2 means relative to the end.
It returns the new offset and an error, if any.

nodes.Name: Truncate
nodes.DocComment:
Truncate changes the size of the named file.
If the file is a symbolic link, it changes the size of the link's target.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

nodes.Name: Remove
nodes.DocComment:
Remove removes the named file or directory.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

nodes.Name: chmod
nodes.DocComment: See docs in file.go:Chmod.

nodes.Name: Chtimes
nodes.DocComment:
Chtimes changes the access and modification times of the named
file, similar to the Unix utime() or utimes() functions.
A zero time.Time value will leave the corresponding file time unchanged.

The underlying filesystem may truncate or round the values to a
less precise time unit.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

nodes.Name: Pipe
nodes.DocComment:
Pipe returns a connected pair of Files; reads from r return bytes
written to w. It returns the files and an error, if any.

nodes.Name: Link
nodes.DocComment:
Link creates newname as a hard link to the oldname file.
If there is an error, it will be of type *LinkError.

nodes.Name: Symlink
nodes.DocComment:
Symlink creates newname as a symbolic link to oldname.
On Windows, a symlink to a non-existent oldname creates a file symlink;
if oldname is later created as a directory the symlink will not work.
If there is an error, it will be of type *LinkError.

nodes.Name: Chown
nodes.DocComment:
Chown changes the numeric uid and gid of the named file.
If the file is a symbolic link, it changes the uid and gid of the link's target.
A uid or gid of -1 means to not change that value.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

On Windows or Plan 9, Chown always returns the [syscall.EWINDOWS] or
[syscall.EPLAN9] error, wrapped in [*PathError].

nodes.Name: Lchown
nodes.DocComment:
Lchown changes the numeric uid and gid of the named file.
If the file is a symbolic link, it changes the uid and gid of the link itself.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

nodes.Name: Chown
nodes.DocComment:
Chown changes the numeric uid and gid of the named file.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

nodes.Name: Chdir
nodes.DocComment:
Chdir changes the current working directory to the file,
which must be a directory.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

nodes.Name: setDeadline
nodes.DocComment: setDeadline sets the read and write deadline.

nodes.Name: setReadDeadline
nodes.DocComment: setReadDeadline sets the read deadline.

nodes.Name: setWriteDeadline
nodes.DocComment: setWriteDeadline sets the write deadline.

nodes.Name: checkValid
nodes.DocComment:
checkValid checks whether f is valid for use, but does not prepare
to actually use it. If f is not ready checkValid returns an appropriate
error, perhaps incorporating the operation name op.
